Decent gameplay and interesting plot since you play the bad guy, kinda reminds me of the Black Company book. But the UI is not very good and even thou there is not a lot of info on screen you kinda have to hunt for the information you need on the battle screen. While the over-world screen lacks any info at all and it seem very barren UI-wise. All the icons and pictures in game are very dark which makes them hard to look at and discern any features. Also all descriptions are very sparse, I would like more lore, about the characters and the overall world and the setting. Don't be shy about describing your world some more, it can be very immersive for the player, at least the one that likes to read. :-) Look at Vagrus and its description of encounters, places and events... Overall a promising game but needs some UI love and more world building.

I wish there was a way to post reviews without giving an "up" or "down". I've finished the short campaign twice and here are my thoughts: The good: - The pixel graphics are great. - Unit and enemy variety is wonderful. - The "Disposable" feature is quite helpful at helping the player not feel sad about losing units. The bad: - There are front line units that buff their allies with an infinitely stackable shield that lasts the entire fight. When I've finished the demo for the first time, I've been trying to focus the squishy targets in the back lines these guys tend to protect, which turned out to be a bad idea. Maybe I'm being stupid here, but this feels like a counter-intuitive design, especially since those squishy targets tend to do a lot of damage or offer utility. - The same stackable buff somehow affects True Damage from DoT effects (The Knight-Archer unit), which is supposed to ignore such things. - Damage and DoT effects are kings. Like, what's the point of leveling up defensive and utility skills of units, when simply upping the damage wins the fight? In this demo, utility skills feel like a trap due to the stackable nature of buffs your enemies have. Killing them quickly ends up leaving you with units that have much more health than playing defensively. - Random level rewards, coupled with a complete reset after the mission, feels like an obnoxious tease. I fail to understand how the random currencies, combined with a kinda random roster of available units is any fun. It's closer to rogue-likes than strategy. - The map feels... weirdly obsolete. You're presented with a choice, but it feels like no choice. Like, there're multiple pathways available, but the game doesn't restrict or punish you for backtracking, meaning that you would always want to get the most before the final fight. I dunno, but to me it feels the same if the game would've had a series of scripted encounters. And what's more, it appears there are permanent rewards scattered here and there for your hero, but if you engage in the final battle of the map - you won't be able to get them. This would've been fair if the final encounter would've been labeled as such, but in the last map it looks just like any other before it. Other: - For some reason, the good guy units you're dealing with have portraits like they're brigands or something. It's not the first time I see things like this, but I always find it weird. - English localisation is lacking. There's nothing egregious about it, but the way character dialogue is written feels off. If the dev team has a trusted linguistic professional - I'd recommend going through the text with them. Like, I'm not trying to bash the game or anything, and I really enjoy playing as a badass villain knight, but I think that some things might damage the game or detract from the experience in the long run.

Great extended demo/prologue, enjoyed pixel art, enjoyed the aesthetic and premise. Had a few stuttering and general performance problems, mostly when loading in to battle but I am using an older machine so it is withing expected margin of error. The UI did it's job, nothing especially good worth praising, but also nothing bad enough to worth mentioning, have seen better, have seen MUCH worse. Regarding the Lord trait picked at the begging of the run, I really hope in the full game there will be more then 2 available to choose from as it is a solid way to diversify runs and with the number of potential strategies available even without them it could massively increase the games replayability. Although I feel like of the 2 available in this demo/prologue, one is clearly better then the other, could use some balancing adjustments to make both attractive picks for a run then just 1 sticking with the 1 that offers you better overall numbers when you do the math. Main "complaint" I would bring up is that I feel unit healing is way to sparse in general, I can understand the lord being hard to heal, but having all my Dread Knights (favorite unit btw) be stuck at about 30-50% HP was infuriating especially with there rather schizophrenic design where they have self armor and thorns like they are tanks, but there stat line is not only that of a DPS, but for some reason they have base HP of only 80 where as the knight archer has like 100 I think. A back line unit who isn't even particularly well armored is more durable then a knight in full plate armor, if that isn't an immersion break I don't know what is. Another thing is I feel gold sources are a bit to scares, I can understand only certain nodes giving gold but why does winning a battle not reward you any? Isn't it common sense to loot the bodies for valuables after you have finished butchering the goody-two-shoes? Incredibly personal pair of pet peeves, why does the dialog auto progress and there is no option in the settings to stop it from doing so, and why does clicking or pressing space on dialogue instead of completing the current dialog box so you don't have to wait if you read fast just skips it? For the records these are observations after a single full run where I beat the final boss. Overall I would recommend the game and have already whitelisted it. but it could still use more work and serious polish.

Fantastic tactical RPG/roguelike where you're the bad guy, so have no qualms losing units for the greater EVIL! This free prologue literally could not be a better deal! Lots of build crafting to explore, and the build aspect is very low on RNG and high on options, so it's pretty easy to try different strategies from run to run. Build options include: - inviting various unit types to ally with you (as opposed to just being mercenaries, which can't be upgraded or hired as easily); - investing in upgrades associated with your allied unit types (which all have a few possible abilities, passives, etc, that can combo between themselves and relics in interesting ways that feel good to pull off!) - hiring units and mercenaries; - gathering powerful and interesting relics; - growing your leader unit (a huge badass that can jump in front of your reg army to save the day and slaughter the opposition, at will! His health doesn't auto regen between battles though, so careful!) All in all, a great and free build crafting tactical wargame! Once I beat it, I'm sure I'll be hitting up the full length paid version cuz they earned it IMHO!
